name: Disagree and Commit
definition: Constructive confrontation is essential to good decisions. Leaders challenge openly when they disagree. We do not compromise for social cohesion. Once a decision is made, we commit fully to ensure a successful outcome. Post decision, proponents and opponents are indistinguishable.

rows.situation: When you are the only one who disagrees
rows.under: Stays quiet and lets the room converge.
rows.justRight: Says the disagreement plainly, with the reason, while the decision is still open.
rows.over: Reopens the argument in every meeting until the room stops inviting you.

rows.situation: After a decision goes against you
rows.justRight: Commits fully. Nobody watching can tell which side you argued.
rows.over: Commits so completely that you never flag the new evidence that the decision was wrong.

rows.situation: When the group wants the meeting to end
rows.under: Trades the right answer for a comfortable room.
rows.justRight: Accepts the discomfort. Cohesion is not worth a decision the company will pay for.
rows.over: Manufactures conflict to prove independence and burns the room's patience.

rows.situation: When the person you disagree with runs your organization
rows.under: Softens the point until it carries no information.
rows.justRight: Makes the case once, clearly, in their terms, and lets them decide.
rows.over: Turns every disagreement into a test of whether you are being listened to.

rows.situation: When someone junior disagrees with you
rows.justRight: Draws the argument out, and makes it safe to have been the one who said it.
rows.over: Reopens your own settled decisions every time anyone objects, so nothing stays decided.

rows.situation: When the facts change after the commitment
rows.under: Sticks to the plan because it was agreed.
rows.justRight: Brings the new facts back and asks for the decision to be made again.
rows.over: Calls every inconvenience new evidence and relitigates the same choice.
